draft.title: Domain and range
card: the set of x values a function can accept. The range is the set of y values it produces.
You cannot take the square root of a negative number. So the expression under √ must be 0 or more. For y = √(x − 2), x − 2 ≥ 0, so the domain is x ≥ 2.
You cannot divide by zero. So any x that makes the denominator 0 is left out. For y = 1/(x − 3), the domain is all real x except x = 3.
Look at the smallest and largest y values the graph reaches. A square root is never negative, so y = √(x − 2) has range y ≥ 0.
draft.remember: Domain is the x values that work. Range is the y values that come out.

a.q: What is the domain of y = √(x + 5)?
a.why: The expression under the root must be 0 or more, so x + 5 ≥ 0, which gives x ≥ −5. The option x ≥ 5 comes from ignoring the sign when moving 5 across. The option x > −5 leaves out x = −5, but √0 = 0 is allowed.
a.clue: Make the expression under the root 0 or more, then solve.

b.q: What is the domain of y = 4/(2x − 6)?
b.why: The denominator is 0 when 2x − 6 = 0, so 2x = 6 and x = 3. Only x = 3 is excluded. Choosing x = 6 forgets to divide by 2.
b.clue: Find the x value that makes the bottom equal 0.
